description: record_callable_shape_surface_publications ignores its surface_shapes param (let _ = surface_shapes). The 4 callers compute it via callable_surface_shapes_for_demand -> surface_shape -> generic_shape_from_demand, which RECORDS callables into delta as a side effect. So removing the param cleanly requires proving that side-effect recording is unneeded (or independently triggered) -- needs oracle validation, not a quick edit. Deferred; do not remove the param without confirming the recorded callables are not consumed by the plan.

comments.text: INVESTIGATED -> NOT REMOVABLE (load-bearing). Empirically removed the surface_shapes param + the 4 callable_surface_shapes_for_demand computations and ran the guards: shadow + filtered contract green, BUT the full lib run made compiler2_transport_plan_scopes_enum_predicate_callback_inputs_to_concrete_activations flaky (passes alone, fails under the full run) -- the 114-vs-19 shape-agreement-conflict family. So callable_surface_shapes_for_demand's side effect (it records callables into delta via generic_shape_from_demand) IS consumed: those records keep the recursive enum-predicate reducer's input shapes from conflicting at solve. The param is ignored by record_callable_shape_surface_publications, but the caller's computation is not -- the ignored result is just how the side effect is triggered. Reverted (green at 56dca5970). A future clean refactor would make the side effect explicit (record the callables directly rather than discard a surface_shapes result), but that needs to identify exactly which records matter -- larger + oracle-gated, not a remove-unnecessary pass.

title: Investigate dead surface_shapes param in record_callable_shape_surface_publications
